title: CalCardo
tagline: An AI calendar assistant that turns chats, syllabi and emails into events you approve
summary: CalCardo was my first big full-stack project that I took all the way from an idea to a live website. You could type something like "lunch with Jack next Tuesday at one", upload a syllabus, or let it find events in your Gmail, and it would suggest calendar events for you to approve before they went into Google Calendar.

hero.alt: CalCardo title beside a calendar icon and the phrases talk, review, and sync
hero.caption: Tell it what's happening, check what it suggests, then sync it to Google Calendar.

sections.heading: Why I built it
body: I had the idea during my first year at RIT. Campus events were spread across emails, apps and flyers, and it was really easy to miss things. I wanted one place that caught all of it, and I wanted adding an event to feel like sending a text instead of filling out a form.

sections.heading: Talking to your calendar
body: The main feature was CalChat. You tell it what's going on and it suggests changes, but nothing actually changes until you hit apply. That mattered to me, because an assistant that quietly moves things around on your real calendar is worse than no assistant at all.
It could move an existing event, create a few events from one message, and even change a recurring event, like ending my swim practice a week early.

media.alt: CalChat showing an existing lunch beside a suggested change to move it and update its description
media.caption: Moving a lunch. Nothing changes until I hit Apply update.

media.alt: CalChat showing separate pending drafts for a walk in the park and lunch with a friend
media.caption: One message, two new events to add or dismiss.

media.alt: CalChat proposing that a recurring swimming event end one week earlier
media.caption: Ending a recurring swim event a week early.

sections.heading: Finding events in your email
body: You could also connect Gmail. When an email looked like it had an event in it, CalCardo pulled out the date, time and place and put it in an inbox for you to accept, edit or ignore. A cheap filter ran first, so the AI only looked at emails that actually seemed calendar related.
Everything synced both ways with Google Calendar, so you could keep using Google's app like normal.

sections.heading: How I built it
body: The frontend is React and TypeScript, the backend is Python and FastAPI, and Supabase handles accounts, the database and file storage. I wrote the early versions myself and then used AI a lot to get it polished enough for friends to test. What worked best was treating the AI like another intern: give it one piece at a time, enough context, and a way to check its work.

sections.heading: Why I paused it
body: Getting Google to approve full Calendar and Gmail access was a long, tedious process, and around the same time the big AI apps started letting you chat with your calendar too. CalCardo still did a few things better, like the review inbox, but not enough to keep going, so I moved on to other ideas. The website is still up but the backend is off. The demo video shows the whole thing working.
